rationale: Both candidates did deep, well-grounded verification with specific file:line citations and largely avoided fabrication; both thoroughly re-examined the hardware/platform-compatibility thread that dominates the ground-truth discussion. X pulls ahead on recall because it also dug into the 'Live Runner State and Ownership' concern (ground truth's #2, ownership of connector-signal draining) and found a genuine gap in the fix (other call sites also drain get_omni_connector_output), whereas Y validated that section as correct but never probed it further. Y's XPU/MUSA device-type-gating and unscoped vllm-serve-example findings are excellent additions to the hardware-compat thread but don't cover new ground-truth territory the way X's ownership finding does. Neither candidate touches the dependency-conflict/mkdocs-build concern, capping both recalls similarly on that axis.
